To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

zinc absorption from the small intestine of the chick is reduced by soy protein but not by casein, that the effect of soy protein is due to a reduction of zinc availability and not to an alteration in intestinal transport mechanisms, that zinc absorption from soy protein is improved by the addition of chelating agents, and that soy protein reduces zinc absorption in the duodenum, jejunum and ileum.

the effect of dietary protein source and level on growth performance of broilers was not significant, but the effect of dietary zinc level on growth performance and carcass yield of broilers was significant.
the dietary protein source affects the absorption and excretion of zinc along the alimentary tract of growing chicks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of protein source on zinc metabolism in growing chicks.
a study of the effect of dietary protein source and level on zinc absorption along the intestinal tract.
the effects of dietary zinc on the absorption of iron, calcium and phosphorus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of dietary protein source and level on growth performance and nutrient utilization of broiler chickens is complex and depends on a number of factors, including the age of birds, the type of protein, the level of protein, the amino acid composition of protein sources, and the interaction of protein sources with other nutrients.

the zinc in animal proteins is more readily absorbed than that in plant proteins, but that this difference is not due solely to the protein source but is also related to the calcium content and the amount of phytate in the diet.
the effect of dietary protein source upon the availability of zinc to the growing chick is dependent on the level of calcium in the diet, the amount of phytate, and the level of zinc in the diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protein source in the diet has a profound effect on zinc absorption along the intestinal tract of growing chicks.
zinc deficiency in the chick can be overcome by feeding a diet containing 1% of soy protein, but that this protein is not as effective as casein in preventing the deficiency symptoms.
the zinc absorption in the small intestine of the chicks was not influenced by the source of dietary protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zinc absorption is affected by the protein source in the diet.
the protein source can have a significant effect on the bioavailability of zinc.
zinc is a very important nutrient for our health, and it is important that we get it from food.
